text:
Taylor: quick sync - we have to land the base-image rebuild plan this week. main blockers: KMS signing flow, who can approve key promos, and how runtime verifies SBOM+signature.
Mira: Agree. For customers on-prem we need an offline signing story. propose: primary path uses cloud KMS (cosign), fallback is signed bundle via operator-run key with recorded fingerprint.
Devon: Fallback is OK but must be auditable. if we allow operator keys, we need a per-customer allowlist and audit entries pushed to central logging. no opaque private keys.
Jordan: From ops: can we expose a single signing API endpoint (signer-service) rather than having CI call KMS directly? would simplify RBAC and reduce key access.
Taylor: signer-service sounds cleaner. responsibilities: accept image digest+sbom ref, call KMS to sign, emit attestation, push signature to registry, and write a structured audit event.
Mira: What fields in audit event? suggestion: {image_digest, image_tag, sbom_sha256, builder_job_id, signer_service_request_id, kms_key_id, commit_sha, timestamp, environment}.
sec-bot: created ticket SSEC-3150 - "implement signer-service + structured audit events" :white_check_mark: https://issues.internal/SSEC-3150
Devon: RBAC matrix idea: CI pipeline SA -> can submit sign requests to signer-service in staging only. Release managers group -> can request prod signing. KMS key admin -> limited to sec team. document ops escalation for key rotation.
Jordan: How to handle revocations? if key rotates or is compromised we need verifier to consult revocation store. runtime verifier should reject images signed by revoked key ids.
Mira: Revocation store could be a signed list in GCS/secure store, pulled at verifier startup and periodically refreshed. need TTL and fallback behavior if store unreachable.
Taylor: Fallback behavior: if verifier can't reach revocation store, fail-safe should be conservative (reject) for prod; permissive for staging. record metric and alert.
Devon: Also include a short-lived grace window during rotation: when rotating prod keys, we allow both old and new keys for N hours and mark rotation event in audit logs with approver id. after window, old key added to revocation list.
Jordan: For private deployments, runtime verifier needs to accept a config for trust roots and an optional offline allowlist. document covenants for customers to publish their own revocation lists if self-hosting.
Mira: SBOM enforcement: in prod we should require SBOM present and matching hash recorded in attestation. If SBOM mismatch, block deploy and surface clear error to operators: "SBOM hash mismatch - possible tampered image".
Taylor: good. add an explicit QA step: verify cosign attestation contains sbom digest in predicate. put sample command in docs.
Devon: sample verify command:\n```\ncosign verify-attestation --attestation /tmp/att.json gcr.io/redwood/base:2026-03-22\njq '.predicate' /tmp/att.json | grep sbom:sha256\n```
Jordan: Scheduling: propose roll window Thu 01:00 UTC. Need sec oncall, platform, and release lead. Also run simulated compromise drill beforehand.
Mira: compromise drill: rotate test key in staging, trigger revocation check, assert verifier rejects old-signed images after revocation TTL. document test steps.
sec-bot: added runbook stub SSEC-revocation-drill to incidents/ for the drill (auto)
Taylor: open question - do we sign intermediate layers or only final manifest? advantage of manifest-only: simpler. advantage of layer-signing: stronger provenance. I lean manifest+attestation that includes SBOM and build metadata.
Devon: manifest + attestation is fine and supported by cosign predicate. avoids signing each layer independently.
Jordan: ops note - registry must support storing signatures and attestations. we're on gcr/artifact-registry which supports OCI attestation; validate retention policies.
Mira: checklist for rollout: 1) implement signer-service in staging, 2) wire CI to talk to signer-service, 3) push SBOMs and attestations to registry, 4) deploy runtime verifier in staging with revocation store, 5) run 1-week canary, 6) rotate keys and run revocation drill, 7) go-live and enable prod-only SBOM enforcement.
Taylor: I'll create the PR with spec and RBAC table. assign @Devon for revocation store, @Jordan for ops runbook, and @Mira for SBOM enforcement text.
Devon: I'll draft revocation store implementation notes (signed JSON file in GCS + pubsub notify). aim PR tomorrow morning.
sec-bot: flagged follow-up SSEC-3150-1: "revocation store design"
Jordan: thanks. small nit - include error codes in runtime verifier for operators: SIGNATURE_MISSING, SIGNATURE_INVALID, SBOM_MISMATCH, REVOCATION_CHECK_FAILED. makes triage faster.
Mira: +1. Also add metric dimensions: verifier_result, key_id, environment, image_repo.
Taylor: great work. we'll reconvene after PRs. :thumbsup:
